messages:
jin: Heads up — found a reproducible memory growth on long-context runs that looks like page-table refcount drift when we run across mixed H100 + RTX pools over NVLink+PCIe.

marta: ack. short description? how to repro?

jin: Short repro attached below. It trips after ~10-15min with 32k seq contexts and repeated streaming. Symptoms: total GPU reserved KV grows steadily, PT walk rate spikes, occasional OOM on the weaker GPU.

jin: repro command:
```
./repro_kvcache --model llama2-7b --seq-len 32768 --kv-cap 48GB --gpu-pool mix-h100-rtx --batch 1 --rounds 2000 --streaming
```

sam: thanks. any dmesg / runtime logs?

jin: pasted snippets (redacted):
```
[2026-07-11T12:03:22Z] kvcache: alloc_page slab_id=7 page_addr=0x7ff12a0000 refcnt=1
[2026-07-11T12:03:22Z] pager: page_table_walk rate=1.2M/s
[2026-07-11T12:12:07Z] kvcache: free_page slab_id=7 page_addr=0x7ff12a0000 refcnt=2 <-- leak?
[2026-07-11T12:13:45Z] kvcache: evict page_addr=0x7ff12a0000 owner_gpu=H100 dest_gpu=RTX6000 via nvlink
[2026-07-11T12:14:01Z] kvcache: pt_unlink failed refcnt=1 expected=0
```

marta: interesting — pt_unlink showing expected 0 but actual 1. could be aliasing (same physical page mapped twice) or a missed decrement on cross-device remap.

tara: any arch-specific pattern? only on mixes?

jin: so far only on heterogeneous pools or when a page migrates from H100 to RTX via NVLink; pure-H100 runs didn't trigger it. Pure-RTX runs also clean. suspect NVLink xfer code path + tiling/granularity differences.

bench-bot: perf counters: at time of leak, PT WALK SSA misses spike; KV cache slab fragmentation grows by ~3% per minute.

sam: could be our PT coalescing heuristic — we coalesce adjacent 64k tiles on H100 but not on RTX. If a tile gets split/merged during migration, refcounts might get out of sync.

marta: hypothesis: when eviction moves pages across links we do a blind remap + incr ref on dest, but on failure branch we skip decref on src. Need to audit error paths.

jin: I tried forcing the old fallback (no coalescing) by setting REDWOOD_KVCACHE_COALESCE=0 and the growth stopped in quick test (30min). Reproduces reliably with default on mixed pool.

tara: nice find. can you capture a repro with memcheck and the evict trace enabled? add --trace-evict & --trace-pt ops.

jin: started a longer run with 
```
./repro_kvcache --model llama2-7b --seq-len 32768 --kv-cap 48GB --gpu-pool mix-h100-rtx --batch 1 --rounds 10000 --trace-evict --trace-pt --env REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug
```
I'll attach logs when it completes (or OOMs).

marta: also try toggling REDWOOD_KVCACHE_COHERENCE_THRESHOLD to 8192 or 16384 — that's the page aliasing size we use to decide per-page atomic moves vs full remap. If decreasing stops the leak, that'll implicate the remap path.

ops-bot: FYI: started a diagnostic node pool with nvlink tracing enabled (pool id: dbg-mix-01). Avoid production traffic.

sam: if we confirm it's a missed decref on the rollback path we should add assert checks in dev builds and a scripty test that injects remap failures to force the rollback.

jin: quick dump from current trace (trimmed):
```
[evict] src_gpu=H100 page=0x7ff12a0000 tile_flags=COALESCED
[remap] -> try remote_map via nvlink: success
[remap] -> dest_ref++ now=3
[evict] -> update_owner success
[remap] -> write-back step failed (EIO simulated)
[remap] -> rollback: dest_ref-- now=2  <-- missing, dest_ref stays 2 and src_ref wasn't decref'd
```

marta: that log shows exactly the missing decref on rollback. Good catch. Does the allocator rely on ref==0 to free tile metadata?

jin: yes. leak accumulates because free path gated on ref==0 but we leave a stale ref. With repeated remap failures and retries across mixed links, it climbs.

tara: mitigation plan: 1) add robust decrement in rollback path and tests; 2) backport hotfix to dedicated infra; 3) add metric for PT refcount drift to surface early.

marta: agree. also add a short-term config: REDWOOD_KVCACHE_COALESCE=0 for mixed pools until we have fix. Update rollout notes.

sam: I'll own unit tests and injection harness. jin, can you draft a minimal patch?

jin: yes — I'll send a PR with tests + assert in dev build this afternoon.

marta: thanks. please drop the failing trace here once PR is up and tag @tara for rollout signoff. :thumbsup:
